description: Looking for a team full of hardworking, compassionate, and high spirited people? You’re in luck, because we are ASTRA IGNITE. Get ready to know and discover space related topics, such as planets (exoplanets), satellites, extrasolar objects, and disaster response. We are open for many people that are yearning to study for those topics and are also hoping to recommend creative ideas, and problem solving
summary: A Silent Archive Wandering the Moon and Mars is a storytelling project that documents the spacecraft and equipment humanity has left behind on the Moon and Mars, It covers the InSight lander, Phoenix lander, Apollo 11’s descent stage and EASEP, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP and Luna 2. Using NASA’s mission records and archives, the project turns scattered technical facts into a clear, human story, Each object is presented with what it did, what it discovered, and how its mission ended. For example, inSight recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes and revealed the structure of Mars’s crust, mantle, and core before its power ran out. This project matters because these objects are the physical record of space exploration. By marking their stories accessible to students and the public, it encourages curiosity about planetary science and raises awareness of the legacy we leave on other worlds.
details: Project ASTRAS IGNITE focuses on retelling the stories of abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars using a highly interactive and accessible website as a free learning tool to educate people from around the world about the impacts of these equipment, and how they changed the history of space. By making this project, we hope that the people can increase their knowledge about the Moon and Mars space programs, build a deep emotional bridge between the public and space exploration, and change their perspective on why many landers and rovers have been discarded. We believe that ASTRAS IGNITE can benefit space agencies, science education, and global heritage. Beyond inspiring awe, these narratives directly support funding, engineering progress, and space policy. To bring this project to life, we used Visual Studio code for the main base, and added the final, creative details using Canva, Ibispaint, and Procreate. Using these applications, we were able to make drawings of the desired space equipment designs, create our official project logo, and make website assets (digital menu, header). Unlike any other projects, we added responsive hover effects, custom cursor states, and light motion (GIFs) that reward exploration without lagging load times. We also added intentional visuals and depth by using hand-drawn illustrations, and physical textures scanned into digital form.
